title: Periodic Table and Properties - Chemistry - Electronegativity
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does Electronegativity differ from Electron Affinity?
options: Electronegativity is measured in kJ/mol; Electron Affinity is unitless
Electronegativity refers to a bonded atom's ability to attract shared electrons; Electron Affinity is for isolated atoms
Electronegativity decreases across a period; Electron Affinity increases
questions.explain: Electron Affinity is an energy change for a single isolated atom gaining an electron. Electronegativity is a relative measure (no units, Pauling scale) of an atom's ability to pull shared electrons towards itself in a **chemical bond**.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which element is the most electronegative on the Pauling scale?
questions.explain: Fluorine is the most electronegative element (Pauling value ~4.0), meaning it attracts bonding electrons more strongly than any other element.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following bonds would be the most polar?
questions.explain: Bond polarity depends on the difference in electronegativity ($\Delta EN$). Hydrogen is \~2.1, Fluorine is 4.0. The difference is large (~1.9). While O-F involves highly electronegative atoms, the *difference* between them (3.5 vs 4.0) is smaller than H-F.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Identify the element with the lowest electronegativity.
questions.explain: Electronegativity decreases down a group and increases across a period. Cesium is at the bottom-left (excluding radioactive Francium), giving it the lowest ability to attract electrons (it prefers to lose them).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: General trends in the periodic table indicate that:
options: Noble gases have the highest electronegativity
Electronegativity is constant down a group
questions.explain: Nonmetals (top right) have high electronegativities as they tend to gain electrons to fill their shells. Metals (left) have low electronegativities.
